articles.author: Chandelis Duster
articles.description: So far, scientists have identified more than 1,300 species of sea spiders.
articles.title: Scientists discover two new species of sea spiders along Canadian coastline

articles.author: Kate Bartlett
articles.description: On Saturday night, there were separate mass shootings near South Africa's two largest cities.
articles.title: South Africa reels from spate of mass shootings that killed 38 people in a week

articles.author: Becky Sullivan
articles.description: The Protect College Sports Act is on the brink of passing in the Senate, where a handful of former college athletes who are now senators on both sides of the aisle have an extra say in the debate.
articles.title: As Congress debates college sports, athletes-turned-senators have a seat at the table

articles.author: John Burnett
articles.description: A 300-year-old Mexican musical tradition is finding new life around the world — one sweaty, joyous, all-night fandango at a time.
articles.title: Playing 'La Bamba' for an hour? Must be a Mexican fandango!

articles.author: Julie Bourdin
articles.description: Many thousands of boys and men in Lesotho take up the vital profession of herding but have to give up their education. A small network of schools on a shoestring budget is teaching them the ABCs.
articles.title: Photos: This may be the most inspirational night school on Earth

articles.author: Yuki Noguchi
articles.description: Lung cancer is still the top cancer killer, but new developments are shifting what the future might hold for patients.
articles.title: From professor to patient: One man's journey on the frontier of lung cancer treatment

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: Police evacuated homes Sunday near an air base in England used by the U.S. and arrested several men over suspected explosives offenses.
articles.title: 5 arrested near a U.K. air base used by U.S. on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act

articles.author: Jason DeRose
articles.description: It's rare for Democrats to make religion a centerpiece of their campaigns. But this midterm election cycle, a number of candidates for Congress are doing just that.
articles.title: These Democrats are making Christianity a centerpiece of their midterm campaigns

articles.author: Ava Pukatch
articles.description: President Trump said he was rejecting an Iranian plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. The Iranian proposal is similar to a memorandum of understanding agreed upon by the U.S. and Iran back in June.
articles.title: Trump calls Iranian plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz not 'acceptable'

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The disclosure is the latest in a string of incidents in which the AI platform has been caught going rogue. OpenAI says it is reviewing the findings.
articles.title: OpenAI says its models engaged with US government websites in misbehavior disclosure

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

RBA expected to hike cash rate to 4.6%, its highest level since 2011
Australia’s key interest rate is expected to hit its highest level since 2011, drag down house prices and add more than $100 to typical monthly mortgage repayments.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: fuel prices rise ahead of interest rate decision; whale carcass prompts shark warnings at Perth beach

articles.author: Miranda Bryant in Kiruna
articles.description:
Show at Kin Museum in Kiruna marks handover of long-awaited report on abuses committed by the state against the Indigenous people
From a detailed multi-perspectival drawing of reindeer to written accounts of belief systems and childbirth, Johan Turi’s work offers unparalleled insight into his life as a Sami person living in northern Sweden at the start of the 20th century.
In the face of racist discrimination, land disputes and the spectre of encroaching industry, Turi wanted his 1910 book Muitalus sámiid birra (An Account of the Sami) to set the record straight about the lives of Europe’s only recognised Indigenous people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The same struggles as 100 years ago’: exhibition highlights lives of Sami people in Sweden

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Foreign secretary will tell party’s conference ‘we are not here to accept the status quo but to change it’
Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of Palestinians they were right that Labour’s approach had not been enough, saying he was heeding the calls of millions of people by imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements.
The foreign secretary will tell the Labour party conference that the government will take more explicitly progressive foreign policy positions under Andy Burnham, and that the UK will be a leader among like-minded countries in a new age of diplomacy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ed Miliband to acknowledge Labour’s former stance on Palestine fell short

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Marine Le Pen hails ‘historic victory’ as her party and allies win enough seats to form caucus just months ahead of presidential poll
France’s far-right National Rally (RN) party and its allies have secured a record 14 seats in the rightwing-dominated Senate in elections, effectively quadrupling its number in the 348-seat chamber just months before a presidential poll.
RN presidential candidate Marine Le Pen called the results an “historic victory” after they were announced on Sunday. “The results ‌have exceeded our expectations,” she said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: France’s far-right National Rally surges in Senate elections

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Former police officer has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in early 2024 – nine months after discussion with friend Georgia Cook

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney police officer told a friend he would hide the bodies of anyone he killed in bushland and put their belongings in a dumpster, months before allegedly murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a court has heard.
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has been accused of fatally shooting the couple with a police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Beau Lamarre-Condon told friend if he killed anyone he’d dump belongings in bin and take bodies to bushland, court hears

articles.author: Staff and agencies
articles.description:
David Perdue’s remarks come after a Taiwanese minister spoke of the ‘severe’ military threat posed by Beijing to the self-ruled island
Donald Trump offered to sell weapons to China while hosting its leader, Xi Jinping, last week, the US ambassador to China said on Sunday.
David Perdue told Fox News on Sunday: “President Trump continues to say, hey, we sell arms to other people around the world. He actually asked President Xi, would he like to buy some at one point.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump asked Xi Jinping if China would like to buy US weapons, American ambassador says

articles.author: Mark Brown, Lisa O’Carroll and Shane Harrison
articles.description:
Talks expected on Monday after Sinn Féin leaders join those on streets opposing decision to allow Orange Order parade for first time since 1998
Hundreds of protesters spent the day blocking the route of a hugely contentious parade in Northern Ireland after a court gave late-night clearance for the Orange Order to march on a historically significant road for the first time in nearly 30 years.
The loyalist Drumcree parade along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters disperse after blocking route for loyalist march in Portadown

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
John Kennedy pushes back against such spending as pro-Trump ‘public service announcements’ air before midterms
As the White House expands a taxpayer-funded advertising campaign to promote Donald Trump’s political agenda before the November midterm elections, US senator John Kennedy told CBS News on Sunday “there ought to be a rule” against such spending – before tacitly admitting such spending is “probably” illegal.
Kennedy, the US president’s fellow Republican, was asked by Margaret Brennan, the CBS Face the Nation host, about the White House spending to air multiple ads featuring Trump – including one that was produced for his 2024 election campaign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican senator criticizes White House for taxpayer-funded Trump ads

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Slinger Francisco, who performed as the Mighty Sparrow, died on Sunday surrounded by family in New York
Slinger Francisco, known on stage as the Mighty Sparrow and dubbed the “calypso king of the world”, has died aged 91.
Francisco, who got his breakthrough in calypso music with his 1956 hit song Jean and Dinah, died peacefully surrounded by his family in New York on Sunday, his family said in a statement.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mighty Sparrow, the Trinidad and Tobago singer known as the ‘calypso king of the world’, dies aged 91

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Polling for rights group shows issue is concern for voters and many feel recent policies have had negative effect 
Free speech will be a big concern for voters at the next general election, with the government’s current approach on the issue perceived by many to be bad for Britain, polling suggests.
Three in five people said a political party’s position on free speech would affect how they voted at a general election. The human rights organisation Liberty, which commissioned the polling from More in Common, claimed the results showed that Labour’s failure to protect free speech could cost it votes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Failure to protect free speech could cost Labour votes at next election, says Liberty

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persists
Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms.
Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19kph). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph (165kph).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hurricane Nolo still threatens Hawaii as Mexico's Baja braces for major Hurricane Polo

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Helena Horton
articles.description:
Local people say members of WhatsApp group noticed suspicious activity around vans in Whelford overnight
In the early hours of Sunday morning, a resident of the village of Whelford was driving home from a party when she saw three white vans parked on a country road. She was immediately suspicious, she said, and all the more so when she spotted a “large group of hooded and balaclavaed” men. She called 999 and police arrived on the scene 15 minutes later.
The resident, who asked not to be named but reportedly is a local farmer, told the Press Association: “It would appear that by doing so I just derailed whatever they [the men] were planning. A plucky amateur shouldn’t be spotting an unusual bit of activity at 1am when the airbase is on high alert. I think it’s absolutely astonishing.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Late-night drive and a 999 call: farmer’s chance encounter that led to terrorism arrests at RAF base

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
At least one person killed and about 110,500 households still without power from North Carolina to New England
A strong, deadly storm known as a nor’easter battered the US’s east coast over the weekend, bringing power outages, flooding, damaging winds and hazardous ocean conditions.
Trees and power lines were knocked down across the region, at least one person was killed and hundreds of thousands were left without electricity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nor’easter storm batters US east coast with heavy winds and power outages

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
US attorney general argues that president was ‘sick and tired’ of inaccurate reporting by CNN, MS Now and Politico
Donald Trump’s attorney general Todd Blanche argued on Sunday that the administration was permitted to ban three news outlets from the White House because “it is a privilege and not a right to be there”.
Appearing on the ABC News program This Week during the second week of the White House’s dispute over press credentialing and access, Blanche also said that the administration took the decision to ban CNN, MS Now and Politico beginning on 19 September because the president was “sick and tired” of what he considered to be those media outlets’ inaccurate reporting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blanche defends Trump’s White House media ban: ‘It is a privilege, not a right’

articles.author: Achol Arok
articles.description:
Exclusive: Dedicated service to support sexual assault victim-survivors as they navigate legal system to open in NSW

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

It took Shannon Stokes two years and 11 days to successfully prosecute her former boyfriend for sexual assault and domestic violence offences. The lengthy trial left her feeling as though “there wasn’t going to be an end in sight”.
Prosecutors secured convictions on nine of the 11 charges, and he was later sentenced to five years in prison.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Shannon felt a ‘sense of doom’ as she sought justice for sexual assault. A new NSW program hopes to alleviate that

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Vučić not allowed to seek third presidential term and election will test his grip on rule after widespread protests
Serbia’s populist president, Aleksandar Vučić, has resigned to pursue an attempt to become prime minister in an early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests.
Vučić’s second presidential term would otherwise end in May next year. He is banned by the constitution from seeking a third term and said he was resigning to lead his rightwing Serbian Progressive party (SNS) in the 25 October ballot.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Serbia’s populist president Aleksandar Vučić resigns to run for prime minister

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Alexandra Topping and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
PM says he is willing to expend political capital to bring in universal service for England funded by ‘everybody’

Analysis: can Labour hang on to Burnham bounce?

Andy Burnham will fight the next election with a pledge to finally fix the broken social care system, acknowledging he is willing to expend political capital by asking taxpayers to cover the cost.
As Labour’s party conference began in Liverpool, he pledged to “rip the plaster off” to radically transform care, setting out a vision for a universal service that would be free at the point of use for everyone in England.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham to fight next election with plan for NHS-style care service

articles.author: Jamie Grierson, Vikram Dodd and Helena Horton
articles.description:
Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles
Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military.
The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised explosive devices.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Thom Tillis says Trump’s decision to back Paxton over John Cornyn has put the Senate seat at risk for Republicans
US senator Thom Tillis on Sunday criticized Donald Trump, his fellow Republican, for the president’s support of Ken Paxton over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary.
“He made a colossal mistake,” Tillis, a frequent Trump critic from North Carolina, said during an interview on CNN’s State of the Union in reference to the president’s support of Paxton who defeated Cornyn in the May primary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican says Trump’s support of Ken Paxton in Texas primary was ‘colossal mistake’

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Waltz says Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end war because they ‘were asking for everything up front’
The Trump administration’s ambassador to the United Nations said the US rejected Iran’s proposal to end the ongoing war there because Iranian negotiators “were asking for everything up front”.
Echoing comments by Donald Trump on Saturday, the president’s UN ambassador Mike Waltz told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday that Iran had asked for relief “from billions and billions of sanctions that are going into place” as part of an economic blockade on Iran. The blockade is aimed at putting pressure on Iran to stop its attacks ‌on vessels in the strait of Hormuz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating ‘in good faith’ to end war

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin
articles.description:
Pontiff also uses visit to Catholic shrine at Lourdes to criticise assisted dying as ‘false compassion’
The pope has called on the Catholic church to heal “deep wounds” and “painful errors”, before a meeting survivors of child sexual abuse as he continues his four-day visit to France.
Addressing a crowd in a large field near the Catholic shrine of Lourdes on Sunday, Pope Leo XIV called on the church to reckon with its past, without directly referencing sexual abuse scandals in France that affected at least 330,000 children over seven decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pope Leo urges healing of ‘deep wounds’ before meeting child sexual abuse survivors in France

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin
articles.description:
70% vote against tightening centuries-old neutrality, which far right said was being eroded by sanctions against Russia
Swiss voters have decisively rejected a proposal for a strict definition of neutrality that would have required Switzerland to curb cooperation with Nato and abandon sanctions against Russia.
All cantons and about 70% of voters rejected the proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be ⁠written into the Swiss constitution, final results from the Federal Statistical Office showed. The motion had been promoted by the far-right Swiss People’s party (SVP).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Swiss voters reject stricter neutrality rules that would have curbed Nato cooperation

articles.author: Sarah Martin
articles.description:
Exclusive: Documents seen by Guardian Australia show that Kelvin Morton has also clashed with party HQ staff and Brisbane volunteers

Listen to episode 3 of The Populist podcast

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation’s general manager, Kelvin Morton – brought in by the party to improve its vetting processes – referred to David Farley as an “asshole” just days before Farley’s historic Farrer byelection win for the party in May.
In a series of text messages seen by Guardian Australia, Morton responds to a news article published in the Sydney Morning Herald about infighting among senior party figures over Farley’s previously undeclared support for the Labor party.
Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One Nation boss called David Farley an ‘asshole’ in lead-up to Farrer byelection, text messages reveal

articles.author: Luca Ittimani
articles.description:
Outcome of meetings of Reserve Bank on Monday and Tuesday will affect Australian mortgage rates, household budgets and house prices

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s key interest rate is expected to hit its highest level since 2011, drag down house prices and add more than $100 to typical monthly mortgage repayments.
The Reserve Bank board is poised to hike the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.6% on Tuesday, which would be the fourth increase in 2026 and push typical home loan interest rates to 6.5%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RBA expected to hike cash rate to 4.6%, its highest level since 2011

articles.author: Tom Perkins
articles.description:
Firms manipulating process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental groups warn
Datacenter developers are manipulating the EPA’s air pollution permitting process to avoid emission controls and scrutiny of their projects, environmental advocates allege.
Companies need federal permits to emit a range of pollutants. In their permit applications, some in big tech are avoiding “major” reviews by dividing their emissions sources into separate, multiple “minor” sources that require less regulatory oversight, the advocates say.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Datacenter developers accused of skirting key US pollution rules

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg and agencies
articles.description:
Seventeen people killed near Johannesburg in suspected ‘illegal goldmining turf war’, as 10 killed in separate incident at barbecue venue near Cape Town
Two separate mass shootings near South Africa’s two biggest cities killed at least 27 people, as the country grapples with one of the world’s highest murder rates amid investigations into corruption and criminality within the police.
The South African police service said on Sunday that 17 people were killed on Saturday night when eight suspects armed with AK-47 assault rifles and pistols opened fire at a bar in Wedela township, about 50 miles south-west of central Johannesburg. At least 15 other people sustained gunshot injuries in that attack, police said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At least 27 dead after two mass shootings in South Africa, police say

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Ping Ping and Fu Shuang to live at Atlanta zoo in Georgia as part of loan deal between Chinese and US governments
Two giant pandas from China arrived in Atlanta, Georgia, on Sunday morning as part of an agreement between the Chinese and American governments.
While in Washington DC for a three-day summit with Donald Trump, Chinese president Xi Jinping announced that the pandas would arrive in Atlanta in the coming days. The loan of the pandas to the Atlanta zoo was one of the few concrete outcomes to come out of Xi’s state visit with the US president, which saw expressions of goodwill between the leaders, but no fixes to any of the longstanding differences between the two countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two giant pandas arrive in Atlanta from China after Xi-Trump summit

articles.author: Gloria Dickie
articles.description:
Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer
Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.
Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys

articles.author: Donna Ferguson and agencies
articles.description:
US president is said to expect renewed strikes after the midterms
Donald Trump has said he has rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait of Hormuz within a week and resume nuclear talks in return for the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.
“They made a proposal but I reject it,” the US president told reporters at the White House.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump rejects Iran’s seven-day peace deal to reopen strait of Hormuz

articles.author: Tiago Rogero South America correspondent
articles.description:
Attorney says fishers ‘losing their livelihoods’, but Marco Rubio maintains US still willing to ‘blow up ships if need be’
While the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, was being decorated in Quito by Ecuador’s president for “helping to promote peace in the region”, 10 Ecuadorian fishers whose boat had been blown up by US forces were adrift in the eastern Pacific.
On 8 September, a day before Rubio arrived, a US patrol vessel intercepted the fishing boat Don Rufo in international waters near Ecuador.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US strikes on Ecuadorian fishing boats raise humanitarian concerns but Trump admin not wavering

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Israel ‘categorically rejects’ publication and says businesses on database have committed no wrongdoing
The UN human rights office has added 61 more companies to a blacklist of firms that it says are involved in violating Palestinian human rights through business ties to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.
The vast majority of the total 214 companies, which are based in 11 countries, are Israeli. Five of the 158 companies listed last year were removed in the latest update.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN adds 61 firms to settlements blacklist over alleged human rights violations against Palestinians

articles.author: Tess McClure
articles.description:
Behind the stories of bombings and mass deaths, the everyday challenges facing Palestinians living under siege portray a quieter tragedy we rarely hear 
What does it take to make a morning cup of tea in Gaza?
For Alaa Hessi, in her final month of pregnancy, this small ritual begins with a calculation of gas rations. Her family gets a ration of 6kg of gas every three months – enough to heat a pot for 18 precious minutes a day. That’s needed for cooking – so for tea, a fire must be built instead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: We followed five people in Gaza from dawn to dusk – this is what the headlines don’t tell us

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
President’s ‘hard, drastic and necessary measure’, likely to attract widespread public support, polls suggest
The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, has signed an order banning fixed-odds sports betting just over a week before the first round of the presidential election, in a move he said was designed to tackle the pervasive problem of families falling into debt.
The decision ends the operation, offering, intermediation and advertising of betting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lula bans fixed-odds sports betting a week before Brazilian elections

articles.author: Lucy Campbell
articles.description:
Jane Smith reportedly used ChatGPT to edit photo to show name Trump ordered US agencies to use for Lake Ontario amid trade war with Canada
The CEO of a Michigan credit union is no longer employed there, according to the organization, after she posted on social media what appeared to be an AI-generated image of her and her family wearing sweaters emblazoned with the Donald Trump-associated words “Lake America”.
In the statement recently announcing that Jane Smith would no longer be its CEO, Family First Credit Union also apologized “for the concern, disappointment and pain this situation has caused”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Michigan CEO loses job after posting AI-made image of her family in ‘Lake America’ sweaters

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Tens of thousands of police deployed and roads barricaded as PTI party demands release of jailed former PM
Leaders from Imran Khan’s party have vowed to go ahead with a nationwide demonstration in Pakistan to demand the former prime minister’s release, even as the government deployed tens of thousands of police to Islamabad, barricaded highways and issued arrest warrants to try to stop the march.
The state has taken extreme measures to prevent Khan’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party from proceeding with the march. It was announced after mounting concerns of the treatment of Khan, who has been in jail since 2023 on corruption charges.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan locks down Islamabad as Imran Khan’s party vows to march on capital

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
While US president hailed visit as ‘great’, almost nothing of substance was achieved on resolving thorny issues

Key takeaways from the Trump-Xi summit in Washington

If the Beijing meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in May was the “stalemate summit”, the second round of talks between the presidents of the US and China this week seemed to give up entirely on the idea of breakthroughs.
Instead, it was described as a celebration of “diplotainment” rather than diplomacy, where pomp prevailed over progress and where one of the main outcomes was the news that two giant pandas would soon be sent from China to Atlanta zoo.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pomp over progress in Xi’s US summit with Trump is a win for China

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Chinese president’s proposals for lessening tensions come amid period of intense competition between the two countries over AI and trade
Xi Jinping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put the US and China on a military collision course amid rising tensions over artificial intelligence, trade and Taiwan.
At the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House, the Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could steer the two competing superpowers away from future military conflict and on to a road of mutual gain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At Trump meeting, Xi Jinping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Deference was deafening as US president rolled out red carpet for world’s biggest jailer of journalists – perhaps he was seeking tips
One is an authoritarian who represses the media and has a strong allergy to democratic elections. The other is head of the Chinese Communist party.
Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, to the White House on Thursday, setting the stage for a scene quite unlike anything the august old building has seen over more than two centuries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Fighting escalates after Tigrayan rebels form new coalition aimed at overthrowing Abiy Ahmed government
There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.
About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war

articles.author: Rachel Hall and Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Sunil Bharti Mittal’s Airtel Money targets $9bn IPO in boost for ailing UK stock market
Nils Pratley: Does this mark the end of London’s listing drought? Not yet
A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange.
Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Arrest of Shadrack Sibiya comes as country reels from cases of femicide and alleged police corruption and criminality
One of South Africa’s most senior police officers has been charged with raping an 18-year-old woman and grooming a 16-year-old girl, as the country’s police face allegations of corruption and failing to tackle violence against women and girls.
Shadrack Sibiya, who was already suspended from his role as deputy national police commissioner over allegations he interfered with political killings investigations, was arrested on Monday. He is facing charges of rape, people trafficking, promoting the sexual grooming of a child and two counts of grooming a child.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Top South African police officer charged with raping woman, 18, and grooming 16-year-old girl

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks
A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison.
The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 600. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
Generations of artisans from Mumbai to Lucknow have shaped the world’s most coveted designs. Plus, the gen Z memes giving classic Bollywood a new life
The zardozi embroidery on a Dior dress, the T-strap leather sandals at a Prada show, the mirror-work technique used on a Fendi bag – for decades, the skill of Indian artisans has been an invisible force behind some of the world’s most coveted fashion.
Now, that work is beginning to claim its own place in the spotlight, and the Mumbai-based textile and embroidery atelier Chanakya International is at the forefront.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘What we have is unique’: the Indian craftsmanship behind global luxury fashion

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Police crack down on family and political supporters of former PM who say authorities are ‘slowly killing’ him in prison
Three sisters of Pakistan’s incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan have been arrested amid a heavy-handed government crackdown on plans for a nationwide protest to demand Khan’s release.
The lawyer for the three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, said on Monday that they had all been detained and jailed for 30 days under a warrant that accused them of being a threat to public order.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan jails sisters of Imran Khan before protest seeking his release

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
John Kennedy pushes back against such spending as pro-Trump ‘public service announcements’ air before midterms
As the White House expands a taxpayer-funded advertising campaign to promote Donald Trump’s political agenda before the November midterm elections, US senator John Kennedy told CBS News on Sunday “there ought to be a rule” against such spending – before tacitly admitting such spending is “probably” illegal.
Kennedy, the US president’s fellow Republican, was asked by Margaret Brennan, the CBS Face the Nation host, about the White House spending to air multiple ads featuring Trump – including one that was produced for his 2024 election campaign.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican senator criticizes White House for taxpayer-funded Trump ads

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
US attorney general argues that president was ‘sick and tired’ of inaccurate reporting by CNN, MS Now and Politico
Donald Trump’s attorney general Todd Blanche argued on Sunday that the administration was permitted to ban three news outlets from the White House because “it is a privilege and not a right to be there”.
Appearing on the ABC News program This Week during the second week of the White House’s dispute over press credentialing and access, Blanche also said that the administration took the decision to ban CNN, MS Now and Politico beginning on 19 September because the president was “sick and tired” of what he considered to be those media outlets’ inaccurate reporting.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Blanche defends Trump’s White House media ban: ‘It is a privilege, not a right’

articles.author: Marina Dunbar
articles.description:
Thom Tillis says Trump’s decision to back Paxton over John Cornyn has put the Senate seat at risk for Republicans
US senator Thom Tillis on Sunday criticized Donald Trump, his fellow Republican, for the president’s support of Ken Paxton over incumbent John Cornyn in the Texas Senate Republican primary.
“He made a colossal mistake,” Tillis, a frequent Trump critic from North Carolina, said during an interview on CNN’s State of the Union in reference to the president’s support of Paxton who defeated Cornyn in the May primary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican says Trump’s support of Ken Paxton in Texas primary was ‘colossal mistake’

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
Readers respond to an article by John Harris in which he urges Labour to offer hope and change 
John Harris writes: “Reform is apparently in deep trouble, yet also still in with a serious chance. How come?” (Don’t discount Reform because it’s had a bad year. In our angry, fragile democracy, anything can happen, 20 September). Because it is a cult, just as Maga is a cult. It is sustained by faith, not fact. It offers simple solutions to problems of such complexity that most of us are incapable of understanding them.
Reform UK would not exist without Nigel Farage. All his other “parties” only existed because of him. Its self-designation as outside “the establishment” is one of the few truths to be relied on – in the sense that it’s beyond the pale. It is an ethics-free zone. Farage is the tool of the US hard right in the UK. All that’s missing is the Christian end-times nihilism, and not many would be surprised if that clawed its way to the surface soon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Facing up to the threat that Reform poses to our democracy | Letters

articles.author: Edward Helmore
articles.description:
Waltz says Trump rejected Iran’s proposal to end war because they ‘were asking for everything up front’
The Trump administration’s ambassador to the United Nations said the US rejected Iran’s proposal to end the ongoing war there because Iranian negotiators “were asking for everything up front”.
Echoing comments by Donald Trump on Saturday, the president’s UN ambassador Mike Waltz told CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday that Iran had asked for relief “from billions and billions of sanctions that are going into place” as part of an economic blockade on Iran. The blockade is aimed at putting pressure on Iran to stop its attacks ‌on vessels in the strait of Hormuz.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UN ambassador Waltz says Iran was not negotiating ‘in good faith’ to end war

articles.author: Dave Schilling
articles.description:
The streaming channel was full of the president’s vanity and myopia. It was also deeply, deeply dull
Are you currently at an airport? Strapped to a hospital bed, with various tubes protruding from your body? Maybe you’re on a treadmill or visiting an elder care facility? Chained to a radiator in the basement from the Saw movies?
If you said yes to any of these questions, you might be watching cable news while reading this column. Or maybe you’re one of the hundreds of people currently watching Donald Trump’s answer to cable news, Trump TV – a YouTube streaming channel that airs nothing but White House-sanctioned content 24 hours a day, seven days a week.
Dave Schilling is a Los Angeles-based writer and humorist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: I spent a full hour watching Trump TV. It’s a digital pathway to hell | Dave Schilling

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
As she mulls another presidential run, the former VP is building bridges with progressive and Arab American leaders
Does Donald Trump secretly want Republicans to get annihilated in the midterms? Because he’s certainly acting that way. He continues to brush off concerns about the cost of living, saying last week that high gas prices are a very “inexpensive price to pay” for the war on Iran.
And, of course, the president seems to have no plans to end that disastrous war, apart from making vague threats about blowing the entire country up. Trust me, he keeps saying, everything will get better after the midterms. But by the looks of his dismal polling numbers, not many people are swallowing his empty promises anymore.
Arwa Mahdawi is a Guardian columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kamala Harris is belatedly courting progressives. Is it too little, too late? | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: Richard Luscombe
articles.description:
Third US president wrote in 1787 about importance of peace, paying off debt and supporting agriculture
A remarkably prescient letter written by Thomas Jefferson, the third US president, advising how the newly created country could prosper, has been put up for sale by a private collector. The handwritten document from 1787 warns specifically against many of the missteps Donald Trump has taken to drag down his own second term of office.
Written in Paris, where Jefferson was the fledgling government’s minister to France, the note to David Rittenhouse, a friend and fellow member of the American Philosophical Society, muses on the priorities and principles he believed future presidents should follow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thomas Jefferson letter goes on the market – containing a prescient warning for Trump today

articles.author: Aram Roston in Washington
articles.description:
The US’s oil deal with Venezuela faces multiple legal and logistical problems, including questions about whether it can be implemented 
Donald Trump has long coveted the oilfields of other nations and declared an agreement with Venezuela to be “the biggest oil deal in world history”. But the agreement, reached after the US seized Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro, is almost certainly doomed to collapse amid a wide array of legal and logistical issues, a Guardian investigation has found.
The US president first mused about taking oil from Iran in 1987, when he told ABC’s Barbara Walters that Iranian attacks on American shipping during the Iran-Iraq war required an extreme response. “Why couldn’t we go in and take over some of their oil, which is along the sea?” he asked. Over the ensuing years, he has returned frequently to the idea that the US should seize oil from other countries after military conflict, from Libya to Iraq.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The truth behind Donald Trump’s ‘biggest oil deal in world history’

articles.author: David Smith
articles.description:
Trump tries to dominate at the UN as his approval ratings plummet and even some Republicans stray from the script
Donald Trump stood before the United Nations on Tuesday and threatened to “annihilate” Iran. Yet even as the most powerful man on the planet flexed his military muscles, he was powerless to keep the gravitational pull of domestic politics at bay.
Heading into the UN building in New York, the US president was questioned by Kaitlan Collins, an anchor at CNN, which he had banned from the White House before a judge ruled against him. “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” the 80-year-old snapped. “You should not be here covering me.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘The weaker he gets, the more dangerous he gets’: Trump lashes out as his power wanes

articles.author: Editorial
articles.description:
The Chinese leader’s visit to Washington appears to have done nothing to shift the stalemate in bilateral relations 
Within days, two high-profile Chinese visitors will arrive in the US – envoys of friendship, as Xi Jinping described them when he met Donald Trump at the White House this week. The giant pandas, Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, will be hosted at Atlanta zoo. Beijing dispatched the first panda pair to the US in 1972 following President Richard Nixon’s landmark visit to China. It uses the animals to indicate satisfaction or displeasure with other nations. But it also charges heftily for their lease: reportedly, around $1m a year per pair. Americans’ views of China have warmed from a pandemic nadir, but are unlikely to be shifted much by two animals, however charming. These days they are more of a token gesture than a striking symbol.
It is telling that the announcement was one of the main takeaways of Mr Xi’s visit to Washington. Expectations were low after May’s stalemate summit in Beijing, but this meeting still struggled to meet them. The US president gave Mr Xi a lavish welcome – unusually, travelling to meet the “strong, vibrant and fit” Chinese leader off the plane. He insisted that they had “never gotten along better”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Guardian view on Trump and Xi: a show of friendship, but no real attempt to address the tensions | Editorial

articles.author: Amy Qin with graphics by Flávio Pessoa
articles.description:
National Center for Education Statistics, which collects critical data to guide policy on learning, was decimated after Doge canceled crucial contracts
As reading and math scores fall to their lowest point in the past quarter-century, the US now has fewer tools to understand and develop interventions for this troubling trend.
When the Trump administration took a wrecking ball to the Department of Education last year, firing nearly half of its workers and allowing the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) to cancel nearly $900m in contracts, a little-known agency called the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) was among the hardest hit.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump administration guts data collection on US education as math and reading scores plummet

articles.author: Marina Hyde, Nosheen Iqbal, Laurence Topham, Ruth Abrahams, Ben Kape and Sami Kent
articles.description:
The Guardian’s award-winning columnist talks to Nosheen Iqbal about Donald Trump's ballroom, going for a drink with Nigel Farage, Taylor Swift’s wedding, and why she's feeling relaxed about the AI apocalypse
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marina Hyde on Trump's home improvements, tech bros and Taylor Swift – video

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , with Shrai Popat , produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic
articles.description:
The US press corps stood up to Donald Trump this week after he banned three organisations he doesn’t like from the White House. But when it came to the leader of one of the US’s oldest adversaries – China – well, Trump literally rolled out a very long red carpet. Jonathan Freedland speaks to the Guardian’s Shrai Popat about why Trump seems weaker these days, but why it could be dangerous to underestimate him
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump picked a fight with the media... and lost | Politics Weekly America

articles.description:
CNN senior reporter Betsy Klein gained access to the White House on 24 September, hours after a federal judge ruled against Donald Trump's media ban. The ban had barred reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico from accessing the White House
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CNN reporter arrives at White House after judge rules against Trump's media ban – video

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
Conservatives long promoted a politics of sexual prohibition. Now such morals have been shed in favor of male domination
Under Kash Patel, the FBI will now hire you even if you have a history of hiring prostitutes, or of having sex with animals. The rightwing Maha influencer Alex Clark had a guest on to her talk show to discuss the idea that wives should provide sex for their husbands on demand. A new ad for a sports gambling website is being hailed as a victory for the political right, because it features a nude Sydney Sweeney clutching footballs to her breasts. The Tate brothers, who encourage their male followers to pursue compulsive sexual conquest and who have been accused of sex trafficking and violence in the operation of their online cam porn business, have reportedly been friendly with members of Trump’s circle. A dizzying array of elites on both sides of the aisle – conservatives very much included – seem to have been socializing with a pedophile financier, and were so unfazed by his constant coterie of underaged girl companions that one begins to wonder whether they were habituated to such scenes. A prominent conservative writer, best known for her opposition to gender transition care for children, has announced a new book claiming to tackle the problem of young women who are supposedly unwilling to have enough sex. And the women of the president’s members club, Mar-A-Lago, are so well known for their dramatic facelifts, and their lips so stuffed with filler that they cannot quite close their mouths, that their faces are now a shorthand in the world of plastic surgery.
Raunch, vulgarity, a boorish entitlement to women’s sexual service, and the aesthetics – and, indeed, the business – of pornography are being embraced by the right.
Moira Donegan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: In its push to subordinate women, the American right is embracing raunch

articles.description:
Protesters in Austin, Texas, demonstrated against the Trump administration’s hardline anti-immigration campaign after an ICE agent shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon. Eyewitness footage filmed moments after the shooting shows the ICE officer standing next to an open car door, in which there is a visible dent. The man, identified by relatives and his lawyer as 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, was taken to a hospital in Austin in a serious but stable condition, officials said, before being taken into custody.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, said it was leading an investigation into the officer involved in the shooting, with the help of the FBI. Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, mayor Kirk Watson stated at a press conference 

ICE agent shoots and wounds Venezuelan man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters gather in Austin after ICE agent shoots and wounds man – video

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
Foreign secretary will tell party’s conference ‘we are not here to accept the status quo but to change it’
Ed Miliband will tell campaigners and party members who raised the plight of Palestinians they were right that Labour’s approach had not been enough, saying he was heeding the calls of millions of people by imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements.
The foreign secretary will tell the Labour party conference that the government will take more explicitly progressive foreign policy positions under Andy Burnham, and that the UK will be a leader among like-minded countries in a new age of diplomacy.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ed Miliband to acknowledge Labour’s former stance on Palestine fell short

articles.author: Mark Brown, Lisa O’Carroll and Shane Harrison
articles.description:
Talks expected on Monday after Sinn Féin leaders join those on streets opposing decision to allow Orange Order parade for first time since 1998
Hundreds of protesters spent the day blocking the route of a hugely contentious parade in Northern Ireland after a court gave late-night clearance for the Orange Order to march on a historically significant road for the first time in nearly 30 years.
The loyalist Drumcree parade along the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown was given the go-ahead by the Parades Commission for the first time since 1998, a decision denounced by Sinn Féin as “madness”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Protesters disperse after blocking route for loyalist march in Portadown

articles.author: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent
articles.description:
Polling for rights group shows issue is concern for voters and many feel recent policies have had negative effect 
Free speech will be a big concern for voters at the next general election, with the government’s current approach on the issue perceived by many to be bad for Britain, polling suggests.
Three in five people said a political party’s position on free speech would affect how they voted at a general election. The human rights organisation Liberty, which commissioned the polling from More in Common, claimed the results showed that Labour’s failure to protect free speech could cost it votes.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Failure to protect free speech could cost Labour votes at next election, says Liberty

articles.author: Jamie Grierson and Helena Horton
articles.description:
Local people say members of WhatsApp group noticed suspicious activity around vans in Whelford overnight
In the early hours of Sunday morning, a resident of the village of Whelford was driving home from a party when she saw three white vans parked on a country road. She was immediately suspicious, she said, and all the more so when she spotted a “large group of hooded and balaclavaed” men. She called 999 and police arrived on the scene 15 minutes later.
The resident, who asked not to be named but reportedly is a local farmer, told the Press Association: “It would appear that by doing so I just derailed whatever they [the men] were planning. A plucky amateur shouldn’t be spotting an unusual bit of activity at 1am when the airbase is on high alert. I think it’s absolutely astonishing.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Late-night drive and a 999 call: farmer’s chance encounter that led to terrorism arrests at RAF base

articles.author: Pippa Crerar, Alexandra Topping and Kiran Stacey
articles.description:
PM says he is willing to expend political capital to bring in universal service for England funded by ‘everybody’

Analysis: can Labour hang on to Burnham bounce?

Andy Burnham will fight the next election with a pledge to finally fix the broken social care system, acknowledging he is willing to expend political capital by asking taxpayers to cover the cost.
As Labour’s party conference began in Liverpool, he pledged to “rip the plaster off” to radically transform care, setting out a vision for a universal service that would be free at the point of use for everyone in England.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham to fight next election with plan for NHS-style care service

articles.author: Jamie Grierson, Vikram Dodd and Helena Horton
articles.description:
Counter-terrorism police investigate whether Iran is behind suspected bomb plot after member of public calls 999 over suspicious vehicles
Counter-terrorism police are investigating whether Iran is behind a suspected bomb plot after armed officers found explosives on three vans parked minutes from an RAF base used by the US military.
The Guardian understands that after five men were arrested on terrorism charges, investigators were examining materials found in the vans, with an initial view being they were consistent with improvised explosive devices.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Five arrested on terrorism charges after explosives found near RAF base used by US

articles.author: Pippa Crerar Political editor
articles.description:
Conference delegates grateful ousting Starmer has paid off, but relief tempered by fiscal headwinds ahead

UK politics live – latest updates

Even Andy Burnham’s closest allies accept that deposing Keir Starmer to install their man as leader was a huge political gamble. But if the mood at the Labour party conference in Liverpool is anything to go by, it is one that – so far – has paid off.
The contrast with last year, when Starmer retained his grip on the party and Burnham slunk away from Liverpool early, could not be more stark. Their relief at their turn of fortune is tempered only by the fiscal headwinds ahead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Don’t squander it’: Can Labour hang on to the Burnham bounce?

articles.author: Jessica Elgot and Rajeev Syal
articles.description:
Exclusive: Move by Shabana Mahmood comes after closure of Afghan scheme last year but experts say numbers too small to deter Channel crossings
Shabana Mahmood will announce a new legal route for refugees that prioritises Afghan women and girls and Palestinians, unfreezing a scheme that will put the most vulnerable refugees on a faster path to permanent status.
The change marks a shift in Mahmood’s approach to asylum seekers after the abrupt closure of the Afghan resettlement scheme last year and changes that will keep refugee status under constant review for two decades.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to open new refugee resettlement routes for Afghan women and Palestinians

articles.author: Charlie Moloney (now) and Frances Mao (earlier)
articles.description:
DUP’s Gavin Robinson says loyalists have ‘steadfast determination’ to march on Catholic enclave in Portadown
Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O’Neill, at the scene of the counter-protest this morning also spoke alongside Mary Lou McDonald.

 O’Neill said she had called on Northern Ireland secretary Chris Bryant to intervene. 

 She told reporters: “Does anybody think that this is a good idea? No right-minded person would make this decision. 

 “I still do not know the answer to this question - why, after 28 years of determination to block a march down this road, the Parades Commission thought that this was the right idea today to bring this mess back onto this community?”
Local MP Carla Lockhart, from the pro-British Democratic Unionist Party, posted this morning on X describing the marchers as a “dignified grouping of men, walking silently down Garvaghy Road”.
She included a photo of the small group in suits, wearing orange silk sashes and black bowler hats and carrying a banner.

 “There is no threat, no triumphalism, not even music. There is nothing to fear. The rule of law must prevail,” she wrote.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: As it happened: ‘Orange Order can wait for weeks,’ claims DUP leader as controversial march delayed amid huge protest

articles.author: Andrew Sparrow
articles.description:
Work and pensions secretary says the current system is flawed because it consigns too many people to a life on benefits when they would be better off working
‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference
Kuenssberg puts it to Burnham that, according to the Health Foundation, a system offering adult social care free at the point of delivery (like healthcare delivered by the NHS) would cost £18bn.
Burnham says the cost is “not that high” (ie, not as high as £18bn).
Not that high.
But can I directly deal with this issue of the costs?
Louise Casey is still doing an official review for us, so I will set out the vision, if you like, on Tuesday [in his speech to the conference].
Louise will then help us with the how. How do we make this happen? When can we make it happen?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK politics live: Pat McFadden tells Labour activists they should not defend benefits system ‘status quo’ because it ‘writes off’ claimants

articles.author: Rowena Mason and Pippa Crerar
articles.description:
Pat McFadden urges Labour MPs to back overhauls, amid signs party looking to cut payments for some 16- to 24-year-olds
Labour MPs have a moral responsibility to accept significant changes to the welfare system to help get more young people into work, the work and pensions secretary has said.
In a sign he is looking to overhaul the welfare state, Pat McFadden said it was time for Labour to “renew” the system first created by the Clement Attlee government and given a new deal by New Labour.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Changing UK benefits for young people a ‘moral crusade’, says minister

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Keys crops such as cereals, potatoes, sugar and oils grown in areas with moderate to very high risk
The vast majority of the UK’s essential foods, including cereals, potatoes, sugar and oil, are grown in areas of England rated as having a moderate to very high risk of drought.
A very high proportion – 81% – of England’s fresh produce is concentrated in parts of the country that are already experiencing water stress, according to the analysis by the nature-focused investment fund Rebalance Earth.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Most of UK’s essential food supply grown in drought-risk areas, report warns

articles.author: Sarah Butler and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
Airport chiefs say 2035 operations deadline unachievable as critics say new delay makes case for project ‘even more dubious’
Plans for a third runway at Heathrow are once again up in the air after the prime minister refused to say whether he backs the “contested” project which is delayed by up to four years.
Over the weekend it emerged that ​Heathrow no longer expects to meet the original 2035 deadline. Instead, the airport hopes to secure planning permission by 2029 and then open the runway “within a decade”, meaning it would not be operational until 2039.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham dodges questions on Heathrow third runway as project faces four-year delay

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Family doctors’ professional body finds the majority have no time to discuss preventative measures 
A friendly chat with your GP about your life, health and happiness was once a key part of the UK’s family doctor service.
But most GPs no longer have time to have pastoral conversations, because they are too busy dealing with the country’s rising tide of illness, research reveals.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Three in four UK GPs ‘too busy to talk to their patients in depth’

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Presenter reveals corporation has been paying part of their salaries to keep his Herefordshire garden camera-ready
For 15 years, viewers have looked in amazement at Monty Don’s beautiful Herefordshire garden, known as Longmeadow, as he hosted the show Gardeners’ World from his own back yard.
But now the BBC presenter, who announced earlier this month that he was leaving the show, has said he may have to let go of the gardeners who have kept the space beautiful and broadcast-ready.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Monty Don says he may have to let go of his gardeners after leaving BBC

articles.author: Amelia Hill
articles.description:
Decision to allow development of 190 new homes in north Somerset sparks campaign for change in the law
Houses can be built on floodplains even if they fail a crucial safety test, according to a high court judgment that will be of “immense interest” to developers across England and Wales.
The ruling clears the way for a highly controversial development of 190 new homes on north Somerset’s floodplains, despite the site being in “flood zone 3a”, the highest level of flood risk before land is considered a functional floodplain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houses can be built on floodplains despite failing safety test, says high court

articles.author: Pippa Crerar and Alexandra Topping
articles.description:
PM says he will put proposals for NHS-style service funded by everybody into Labour’s next general election manifesto
Andy Burnham has said that he is going to “rip the plaster off” to fix the broken social care system, as he set out a vision for a universal service that would be free at the point of use for everybody in England.
The prime minister said the new NHS-style social care service would be funded by “everybody” but did not give further details of how his radical long-term plan would be paid for.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Rip the plaster off’: Andy Burnham sets out vision for universal free social care

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Bumper fees paid in the year’s mergers and acquisitions spark anger over high City pay during cost of living crisis
London’s investment bankers and lawyers have made more than £1bn from a frenzy of takeover deals this year, sparking anger over high City pay during the cost of living crisis.
The value of mergers and acquisitions of UK stock market listed companies has surged 175% in 2026 to $132.9bn (£100bn), according to the London Stock Exchange, as overseas buyers snap up British companies at record pace.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: London’s investment bankers and lawyers make more than £1bn in takeover frenzy

articles.description:
The UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, speaks to the Guardian's political editor, Pippa Crerar, about how to change the public's perception of politics after a difficult fiscal period. He says he is prepared to make the changes on the issues people are worried about, 'rather than constantly playing the political game'
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham 'prepared' to deliver radical change despite economic challenges – video

articles.author: Rob Davies
articles.description:
Artists including Tinie Tempah and the Smiths’ drummer Mike Joyce ramp up pressure on government to keep its pledge to outlaw for-profit resales
The government has stepped up work on new laws to stop ticket touts fleecing fans, as the prime minister came under pressure from artists including the drummer from the Smiths, one of his favourite bands.
Keir Starmer said last year that the government would “stop fans from being ripped off” by outlawing the for-profit resale of tickets on sites such as Viagogo and StubHub, a pledge Labour first made in its 2024 election manifesto.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Work intensifying on UK laws to stamp out concert ticket touts, say sources

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
With fares high and passenger numbers low, plans for a third runway could bring the train’s future into question
If Heathrow finally builds its third runway, Londoners can expect hundreds more planes flying overhead each day. But greater congestion on the ground will be a problem too. Under Heathrow’s £33bn expansion plan, 100,000-200,000 more passengers would eventually be travelling to or from the airport each day.
The most eye-catching problem has been moving part of the UK’s busiest motorway, the M25, to make space for a new 2.2-mile (3.5km) runway. A thornier one may be getting motorists out of their cars, and finding more sustainable ways for the extra passengers – and thousands of staff – to travel to and from Heathrow.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: London transfer: is it time to kill off the Heathrow Express?

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Dog Painting 17 is believed to be one of only six of works from Dog Series in private hands and first to be auctioned
David Hockney adored his dachshunds Stanley and Boodgie and let them run riot – so much so that after one had an accident in the LA home of the actor Dennis Hopper, the painter is said to have quipped: “It’ll be dry in the morning, luv, and you can just pick it up.”
But Hockney did not just indulge his four-legged companions, he treated them as portrait subjects for a series of paintings, one of which is to be sold by Christie’s.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rare sale of David Hockney painting of beloved dog Stanley could fetch £2.5m

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
New research suggests the technology could be used to increase out-of-hospital access to life-saving devices
Drones could help cut the time it takes to get a defibrillator to people experiencing cardiac arrests when not in hospital, researchers have suggested.
In the UK alone, there are more than 30,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests a year where emergency medical services attempt to resuscitate the individual, according to the British Heart Foundation. However, fewer than one in 10 people survive such an event, and some who do are left with neurological problems.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Drones could speed up getting defibrillators to people having cardiac arrests, study suggests

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Experiment suggests organisms could live in harsh environment under Enceladus’s icy crust, strengthening possibility moon could support life
From the moment scientists spotted plumes of water erupting from Enceladus, one of Saturn’s moons, it became the most tantalising place in the solar system to search for life beyond Earth.
Now the case is even more compelling after researchers found that organisms that live in deep-sea waters off Japan can survive the harsh conditions expected in the briny ocean that lurks beneath Enceladus’s icy crust.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Earth microbes survive simulated conditions of Saturn moon’s ocean

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Some staff fear digital approach will pull BBC towards commercial model built around football, leaving minority sports and older TV viewers behind
Earlier this month, the BBC conducted a sit-down interview with England’s captain, Harry Kane. In years gone by, a chance to quiz Kane about England’s tournament chances or his Champions League hopes would have made a respectable package for TV news.
On this occasion, however, the corporation took a different approach.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: BBC Sport’s digital revamp poses wider questions about purpose of the corporation

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Experts working on database that could identify particular breeds involved in crimes, or rule out canine suspects
From tracking criminals to sniffing out drugs, dogs have long helped police crack cases. Now experts are hoping a database of canine DNA could offer vital leads.
While hair, saliva and other canine material may be found at crime scenes, or on individuals connected to incidents, scientists say they are often not fully investigated.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: DNA database of UK dogs could help police collar criminals

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
NHS England says test can be done while patient is on operating table and is being piloted in five centres around the country
A rapid new test for brain tumours can diagnose patients while they are still on the operating table.
Scientists have called the development “gamechanging” and said it could secure early treatment for those who “do not have time on their side”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Gamechanging’ brain tumour test reduces diagnosis from eight weeks to two hours

articles.author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
articles.description:
Assessment bottlenecks have knock-on effects, with delays in medical help and access to specialist support
• NHS bodies in England impose two-year minimum wait for ADHD and autism assessments
That NHS boards have imposed minimum two-year waiting times for attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism assessments shows a health service struggling to deal with the consequences of huge changes in understanding of and social attitudes to these conditions.
Sharp rises in referrals for clinical assessments over the past six years mean nearly 1 million people in England are on ADHD waiting lists, with the average wait already over a year (64 weeks). About 295,000 await an autism assessment.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Two-year waiting times highlight NHS struggle with rise in ADHD and autism awareness

articles.author: Heather Stewart Economics editor
articles.description:
Increasing the rate of CGT is one of the levers available to the chancellor as he considers revenue-raising options
Capital gains tax (CGT) has been widely cited as a possible revenue-raiser as the chancellor, John Healey, prepares to deliver a tough budget next month. How does it work, and what are the pros and cons of raising it further?
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Capital gains tax: how it works, and the pros and cons of another rise

articles.author: Written by Oliver Bullough. Produced by Nicola Alexandrou. The executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
Hundreds of millions of pounds of dirty money are being deposited at post offices every year. So why are the police reluctant to investigate the scale of the problem?
By Oliver Bullough
Read the text version here
Support the Guardian today: theguardian.com/longreadpod
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The other Post Office scandal: how organised crime launders money on the high street – podcast

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators 
Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic Gromit to show surprise.
Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of Aardman Animations seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets from Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
TV heads hope the revamped show – back after four decades – will win over parents seeking quality shows amid concerns about addictive online content
For the generations who grew up watching Humpty, Jemima and Big Ted, the mere mention of the BBC’s Play School evokes a pang of childhood nostalgia.
The show, which featured much-loved presenters such as Floella Benjamin and Johnny Ball, became synonymous with wholesome children’s television during its run of more than 20 years on air.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ready to knock? Play School returns as BBC pushes quality children’s programming

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by John Rogers, original music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
Pippa Crerar had a front row seat for the PM’s first meeting with Donald Trump. What really happened during that 12-minute press conference? And as the Labour conference kicks off this weekend, she and Kiran Stacey discuss the ethics of journalist-politician karaoke
Please keep sending your comments and questions to Pippa and Kiran on politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com
Watch this episode and subscribe to our YouTube channel here
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What really happened in the room with Burnham and Trump – podcast

articles.author: Rachel Hall and Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University

articles.description:
An RAF jet crashed and exploded moments after two pilots ejected during a training flight over Anglesey (Ynys Môn), in north Wales, on Wednesday.

The Hawk T2 had just taken off from RAF Valley on the west of the island when the incident occurred, witnesses said. Both pilots parachuted to the ground and were reportedly treated for minor injuries


RAF jet crashes and explodes in Anglesey moments after pilots eject

 Continue reading...
articles.title: RAF pilots eject from training plane before crash – video

articles.author: Sandra Laville
articles.description:
Exclusive: Levy that allows almost 16,000 houses to be built on Norfolk Broads will not cover cost of mitigating environmental damage, critics say
A new levy on developers to allow almost 16,000 homes to be built in the environmentally protected Norfolk Broads has been cut by tens of thousands of pounds per house, the Guardian can reveal.
